subject.title: fix(agents): add timeout to fd and ripgrep search executions

question: Should agent find and grep stop after 60 seconds of total runtime, or only after 60 seconds without helper-process progress?
rationale: Both policies prevent indefinite hangs, but a fixed wall-clock cap can terminate legitimate active searches while an inactivity cap preserves progress at the cost of allowing longer total execution.

options.title: Use inactivity timeout
options.body: Reset the 60-second timer when fd or ripgrep emits meaningful output, retaining forced escalation only when the helper stops making progress.

options.title: Keep fixed wall-clock timeout
options.body: Accept that every local fd or ripgrep execution is terminated after 60 seconds even when it remains active, and add explicit compatibility coverage for that policy.

recommendation.title: Use inactivity timeout
recommendation.body: Reset the 60-second timer when fd or ripgrep emits meaningful output, retaining forced escalation only when the helper stops making progress.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available history-linked contributor for the adjacent fd and ripgrep timeout lifecycle, though final product authority should remain with the agents-area owners.
